To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
for a wide range of p-norm based optimization problems with p > 1, the optimal solutions have the least sparity for almost all measurement vectors and almost all measurement matrices.

for a broad class of general p-norm based optimization problems with p>1, optimal solutions have the least sparseness for almost all measurement vectors and matrices, and thus the optimal solutions have full support.

the least sparsity of optimal solutions to generalized basis pursuit, ridge regression, basis pursuit denosing, and elastic net is attained by all measurement matrices and all measurement vectors, except a measure-zero set, when the parameter $p$ is greater than one, and the optimal solutions have full support.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the $l_1$-norm based minimization problems, such as the LASSO, are the best sparse optimization problems in the sense that the optimal solutions to them are the sparsest for most of the measurement matrices.
for almost all measurement matrix and measurement vector, the optimal solution to $p$-optimization ($0 < p \ne 1$) is as sparse as the solution to $\ell_p^0$-optimization.

for a wide range of p-norm optimization, the least sparsity is achieved for almost all measurement vectors and matrices, and the least sparse solution can be computed efficiently by solving a convex optimization problem.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the adverse sparse properties of general $p >1$-norm based problems are not due to $p$-specific structures of these optimization problems, but rather are a direct consequence of the non-convexity of these problems.
$p$-optimization problems with $p>1$ are less robust to measurement noise and outliers than their $p$-optimal counterparts with $p\leq 1$.

$p$-optimization problems with $p>1$ are not only more computationally tractable than $p$-minimization with $p\le1$, but they can also be more sparse in the sense that they lead to solutions that have the least sparity.
